'''''Muscari botryoides''''' is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant]] of the genus ''[[Muscari]]'' and one of a number of species in the genus sold as '''grape hyacinth'''. It is sometimes grown as an [[ornamental plant]].

The flowers are close together, and are almost totally round. The lower fertile flowers point downwards, while upper ones, usually paler and sterile, point upwards. The flowers are bright blue with white lobes at the end in the wild species, but other colours are available, including white. ''M. botryoides'' is originally from central and south-eastern [[Europe]], growing in open woodland and mountain meadows.<ref name=Mathew1987>{{Citation |last=Mathew |first=Brian |year=1987 |title=The Smaller Bulbs |location=London |publisher=B.T. Batsford |isbn=978-0-7134-4922-8 }}, pp. 126</ref>
[[File:Muscari botryoides in Tashkent Botanical Garden.jpg|thumb|In Tashkent Botanical Garden]]
The name ''botryoides'' is derived from the appearance of a miniature [[cluster of grapes]].<ref name=JohnsonSmithStockdalev>{{Citation |last1=Johnson |first1=A.T. |last2=Smith |first2=H.A. |last3=Stockdale |first3=A.P.|year=2019|title=Plant Names Simplified : Their Pronunciation Derivation & Meaning |location=Sheffield, Yorkshire |publisher=5M Publishing |isbn=9781910455067 |name-list-style=amp }}, p. 101</ref> ''M. botryoides'' is said to be much less invasive than the related ''[[Muscari neglectum|M. neglectum]]'', nevertheless both species are listed as invasive in [[Tennessee]].<ref name="Editor2002">{{cite book|editor=Beth Hanson|title=Spring-Blooming Bulbs: An A to Z Guide to Classic and Unusual Bulbs for Your Spring Garden|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xaoK1pdNymwC&pg=PA86|access-date=24 November 2012|date=1 November 2002|publisher=Brooklyn Botanic Garden|isbn=978-1-889538-54-9|page=86}}</ref>
